doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Getting sticks, a snare and the jelly bean drumset
summary: He gets his first sticks and snare, sits in on his father's job, and is rewarded with drums for finishing books.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: When did you get your first drumset?

Well my father didn’t want me in the business, so like I said I had gotten a pair of drum sticks from a drummer, and then I got a snare drum from another drummer, oh wow. I was on my way. And eventually my father got into a pickle once and needed a drummer. His drummer didn’t show up. So he made the phone call to my mother, and I played the job.
That’s great. That must have been difficult for him.

Yeah, it was difficult, but then he realized that he’s a goner. That’s it. And I played the job pretty well because he was really amazed at what I had picked up from the records, and just observing what was going on from other drummers. There were a few things, like the Latin I needed to brush up on, technique certainly, and reading I couldn’t read at that point. But he eventually did buy me a drumset. It was a jelly bean kit. It was all different colors because every time I finished a book, he would buy me another drum. So we could never find anything that matched, so I had a jelly bean kit. Then he didn’t like that, because he was a real professional, so we traded that in and we got an entry level kit.
He used that as a little initiative to keep your studies up?
